newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares edge up as Western demand appears.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares edge up as Western demand appears.

text.p: Leading Russian shares edged up on Wednesday as afternoon orders from Western investors supported a morning price lift brought on by local buying, traders said.
The Russian Trading System of 23 shares rose 1.31 percent to 331.64 from 327.37 on $26.79 million total market volume.
LUKoil common shares rose to $14.59 from $14.38 at Tuesday's close and UES preferred gained to $0.1850 after $0.1815.
Gazprom rose to $0.643 from $0.613, Surgutneftegaz oil company rose to $0.86 from $0.84 and utility Kolenergo preferred shares rose to $0.193 from $0.178.

"The market has firmed a bit on some Western demand which exerted moral support for Russian buyers," said Rinaco-Plus trader Alexander Lobanov, adding that supplies of shares had become more difficult to find outside of Moscow.
A Gambit Securities trader said the evening Western demand rescued the market from a mid-afternoon dip.
But traders predicted prices would rise over the next few days as the market absorbed news of the pro-reform government reshuffle announced and the second second Russian Eurobond was launched.
"People are taking the news as definitely positive," Lobanov said.
Russia's mark-denominated Eurobond, to be launched on Thursday, will have a volume of at least 1.5 billion marks and a maturity of seven years, lead manager Deutsche Bank AG said on Wednesday.
